topics.topic: Alias character counting, normalization, preservation, and when length is measured
questions: What counts as one character, and is length measured on the submitted string or after any Unicode normalization?
What exactly counts as one character for the 40-character limit?
Must Registry store and return the alias exactly as submitted, or may it trim whitespace or apply Unicode normalization, and is the length checked before or after any such transformation?
What exactly counts as a character, and is the limit measured before or after any Unicode normalization?

quotes:
A value that is present is kept exactly as written; Registry trims and
   rewrites nothing (R0-68).

A present value is refused when it is outside the form State 1 declares,
   at stage (4) of A04 rule 6, every such value named: an alias longer than
   40 characters, counted as Unicode code points (R0-90, M01) — its length
   only, its content being the owner's rule (R0-82); an object kind
   outside `apartment`, `house`, `commercial`, `other` (M02); a floor area not
   greater than zero, a number of rooms below 1, or a floor that is not a
   whole number (M02); a customer language outside `es`, `ru`, `en` (M04).
judgement.why: State 2 says aliases are counted as Unicode code points and preserved exactly as submitted, without trimming, rewriting or normalization.

topics.topic: Validity and semantics of empty, whitespace-only, and absent aliases
questions: Are an empty string and a whitespace-only string valid aliases, and if accepted are they stored distinctly from a project having no alias?
Is an empty alias accepted, and if accepted is it a present alias shown as an empty value or treated as no alias so that the project id is shown instead?
Is an empty string a valid alias, and if accepted is it stored as an alias or treated as no alias?

quotes: An optional value given as an empty string or white space only is absent.

'Correct a project' gives every editable fact of the project: display name,
   alias, customer link and the object — address, kind, characteristics
   (R0-45).

An optional fact the correction does not give is cleared; there is no
   partial correction.
judgement.why: State 2 treats an empty or whitespace-only optional alias as absent, so correcting with it clears the alias rather than storing an empty alias.

topics.topic: Whether identifying alias content is disclosed to the agent
questions: When an accepted alias actually contains a person's name, address or other identifying content, must Registry return it to the agent as the alias rule says, or withhold it to preserve the unconditional personal-data boundary?
When a permitted-length alias contains a person’s name, address or other identifying value, does Registry return it to the agent or enforce the guarantee that no personal data reaches the agent?

quotes:
Registry cannot tell a person's name from any other word, so the agent
projection leaves out the project's display name: the agent works by the
project's id. Room names and artifact pointers stay in it; the owner names rooms
without names or addresses of people, and a producer publishes `uri`,
`payload_ref` and digest without them. Registry does not inspect these values:
the rule binds their writers and is not a check of Registry, and a value that
breaks it is not refused and does reach the agent. Registry's own guarantee
(R0-26) covers every value it holds as `personal_data`.

The owner names a project by its object and work, never by a person: the
customer's name lives in its Customer record. A name such as "Reforma Pedreres
35" still carries a private object's address, which can identify a person, so
the display name is held as `personal_data`: it reaches the owner and a service
cleared for `personal_data` (R0-43), never the agent, and a consumer reads it
when it uses it instead of keeping it. A project may also carry an alias — a
short neutral label the owner gives it, with no person's name, no address and
nothing else that identifies the object or its customer. The alias is the name
the agent sees in its projection and the one a consumer's kept snapshot holds.
Like room names (R0-68), the alias is a rule on its writer, the owner: Registry
does not inspect it, and an alias that breaks the rule is not refused.

A `personal_data` value leaves Registry to the
owner and to a service whose token allows that class (R0-27) — never to an agent
(R0-25).
judgement.divergence: Registry either returns the accepted identifying alias in the agent projection, which the agent and its AI provider observe, or withholds/refuses it to maintain the rule that personal data never reaches an agent.
judgement.why: The texts expressly say a writer-rule-breaking value reaches the agent while also promising that no personal-data value ever reaches an agent.

witness.initial: An active project with no alias is granted to an agent session, and the owner knows the customer's name.
events: The owner sets the project's alias to the customer's name using no more than 40 characters.
Registry accepts the alias because it inspects only its length.
The agent reads the project projection through Cabinet Kernel.
outcomes: Registry returns the accepted identifying alias because the alias is the name the agent sees and a rule-breaking value is not refused and does reach the agent.
Registry withholds or refuses the identifying alias because no `personal_data` value may reach an agent.
witness.observer: The agent and its AI provider
basis:
A project may also carry an alias — a
short neutral label the owner gives it, with no person's name, no address and
nothing else that identifies the object or its customer. The alias is the name
the agent sees in its projection and the one a consumer's kept snapshot holds.
Like room names (R0-68), the alias is a rule on its writer, the owner: Registry
does not inspect it, and an alias that breaks the rule is not refused.
The owner chooses a project in the owner interface.

The agent,
through Kernel, reads a separate minimal projection of a project its session
is granted (R0-46)
with no personal value: id, display name, status, rooms and artifact pointers.

Narrowed by R0-82:
it carries the project's alias when the owner gave one.

questions: What happens when an existing or restored store already contains an alias longer than 40 characters from before R0-90: may Registry start and return it, must the owner replace it, or is the store refused?

quotes:
The alias is at most 40 characters, and Registry refuses a longer one; it is
never cut.

It has
no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its
place on the host, outside Registry (Explicit exclusions), and Registry
starts on it as on any store.
judgement.why: Validation and startup behavior for an existing or restored store are operational rules owned by State 2, not a State 0 product-frame question.

topics.topic: Overlength-alias failure response and request atomicity
questions: What observable failure identifies an overlength alias, and does refusal leave every other field in the same request unchanged?

quotes:
An alias of 40 characters is stored; one of 41 is refused and nothing
   changes.
Every action is atomic: it applies all its changes or none.

An operation that checks stages (3) to (6) of A04 rule 6 checks
  them in that order and answers the first failing stage with every failure
  of that stage (A04 rule 6): its kinds in the order the operation's Errors
  list them, one entry for each failing input or record, each naming the
  field or the identity it concerns.
judgement.why: Later texts identify the failure as an `invalid_request` with `outside_closed_list` naming the alias field and require the entire correction to leave all fields and the revision unchanged.

topics.topic: Write actions to which the alias limit applies
questions: Which concrete actions accept or change an alias, and does the limit apply to project creation, project correction, import, and every other alias-bearing write?
